research_rationale: EO 10718 (22 FR 4632, signed 1957-06-27) has three sections: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of State the authority vested in the President by section 1745 of the Revised Statutes (22 U.S.C. 1201) to prescribe rates or tariffs of fees for official services at embassies, legations and consulates, to designate what are official services, and to adapt the rates to each post; section 2 provides that the order does not itself amend or end existing rates but includes authority to amend, supersede or terminate them and to prescribe implementing regulations; section 3 requires publication in the Federal Register. The Federal Register pages also print Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1957 (abolition of the Reconstruction Finance Corporation) after the order; the dossier inventory treated sections of that plan as clauses of this order, so the inventory is corrected to the order's own three sections. The held original has no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The authority statute is held and has not lapsed: the held U.S. Code text of 22 U.S.C. 4219 (R.S. 1745; formerly 22 U.S.C. 1201) still authorizes the President to prescribe the rates and prints Ex. Ord. No. 10718 in its Executive Documents note; the held eCFR authority citation of 22 CFR part 22 (amended through 2026-10-21) cites E.O. 10718, and a held 2021 Federal Register rule describes 22 U.S.C. 4219 as implemented through Executive Order 10718. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no amendment, revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: Section 2 is itself the order's savings provision for rates in force before 1957 and keeps the Secretary's authority to amend or end them; it is a continuing clause, not an ended one, so no residual from an ended clause exists and none was found in the bounded searches.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end in the original. A search of held texts for the number 10718 finds only the 1989 OFR codification, the 22 CFR part 22 authority citation, the 22 U.S.C. 4219 note and a 2021 Federal Register rule that applies it; none revokes, supersedes or amends it, and the ofr_catalog search returned no hit.
scope_check: The three sections of the order itself are the inventory (overrides replace the dossier clauses that came from Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1957, which is a separate instrument and not part of this order).
independent_command_check: Section 1 (delegation), section 2 (implementing and amending authority) and section 3 (publication) are separate commands; none depends on a date or condition, and none was ended by a later instrument found.
savings_check: Section 2 keeps existing rates in force pending the Secretary action; no ended clause leaves a residual.

research_rationale: EO 10552 (19 FR 5079, signed 1954-08-10) is a one-paragraph delegation: the Civil Service Commission is designated and empowered, without the approval of the President, to exercise the authority vested in the President by the joint resolution of June 29, 1938, 52 Stat. 1246, as amended by the act of June 11, 1954, 68 Stat. 249 (5 U.S.C. 86a), to promulgate regulations under which certain Government employees may be prevented or relieved from working by administrative order. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation. The only later instrument found that acts on it is EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28; held FR original, 44 FR 1055), section 2-101(b), which lists EO 10552 among the orders amended by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; that is an amendment of the named delegate, not an end of the delegation. The held U.S. Code text of 5 U.S.C. 6104 (Executive Documents note) prints Ex. Ord. No. 10552 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12107, and the held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 610 still cites E.O. 10552 as authority. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) were read for coverage and surface no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: The order is a standing delegation of rulemaking authority, not a one-time act, and has no savings clause. Nothing in the held original or in the bounded searches shows a residual or independent command that outlived an ended clause; the clause has not ended.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: the original has no date, condition or sunset. No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the three bounded searches or in a search of the held texts for the number 10552 (hits: EO 12107 list, 1989 OFR codification, 5 U.S.C. 6104 note, 5 CFR part 610 authority citation). EO 12107 amends the delegate name only, effective 1979-01-01.
scope_check: The order contains a single operative paragraph (clause EO:10552#whole). The clause inventory of one clause was confirmed against the held Federal Register text, which is the whole order.
independent_command_check: No independent command: the order delegates one authority only. EO 12107 section 2-101(b) amends it rather than revoking it, and the substance of the delegation (promulgating regulations on preventing or relieving employees from working by administrative order) is unchanged.
savings_check: No savings clause in the original and no surviving residual from an ended clause, because the clause is still operative as amended.

research_rationale: EO 11935 (41 FR 37301, signed 1976-09-02) amends Civil Service Rule VII (5 CFR Part 7) by adding a new section 7.4 (Citizenship): no person shall be admitted to competitive examination, or appointed in the competitive service, unless a citizen or national of the United States, with the Commission authorized to make exceptions to the extent permitted by law for aliens when necessary to promote the efficiency of the service in specific cases or for temporary appointments. The held Federal Register original has no sunset or condition. Later instruments held: EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28), section 2-101(a), lists EO 11935 among the orders amended by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, effective 1979-01-01 under its section 2-404; and the 2020 EO 13940 recites EO 11935 in a compliance-review direction without amending or ending it (a recital, not an end). The held eCFR text of 5 CFR 7.3 (amended through 2026-10-29) reproduces the rule as three paragraphs with OPM in place of the Commission, and its source note reads 'E.O. 11935, 41 FR 37301, Sept. 3, 1976. Redesignated by E.O. 13197, 66 FR 7853, Jan. 25, 2001', a renumbering of the section (7.4 to 7.3) in the codified rule, not a revocation or supersession; the text of EO 13197 is not attached as a later event because it is not an actor text in the packet, and it does not end the rule since the held 5 CFR 7.3 text keeps all three paragraphs. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause and its clause has not ended; the current rule text in held 5 CFR 7.3 continues it, so no residual from an ended clause arises.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end. Searching the held texts for the number 11935 finds EO 12107's list, EO 13940 and Federal Register pages citing it, and 5 CFR 7.3, 6.8 and 29 CFR 1606.5 texts applying it; none revokes or supersedes it. EO 12107 amends the agency name only; the CFR source note records the renumbering by EO 13197; neither ends the rule.
scope_check: The order is one paragraph adding one new section (7.4) of three paragraphs to the Civil Service Rules, treated as one clause (EO:11935#whole), the whole order in the held 41 FR 37301 original.
independent_command_check: Paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of the added section are parts of one rule: the two bars and the exception. Held 5 CFR 7.3 shows all three continuing, so no part ended independently.
savings_check: No savings clause in the order, and no ended clause leaves a residual.

research_rationale: EO 11701 (38 FR 2675, signed 1973-01-24) has five sections: (1) the Secretary of Labor shall issue rules requiring each executive department and agency to list suitable employment openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service, in consultation with the Civil Service Commission; (2) the Secretary of Labor is designated and empowered to exercise, without presidential approval, the President's authority under section 2012 of title 38, United States Code (now 38 U.S.C. 4212); (3) the Secretary of Labor shall gather information on the effectiveness of the program and report to the President from time to time; (4) agencies shall issue procurement rule amendments in consultation with the Secretary and cooperate with and comply with the Secretary's rules; (5) Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971 is superseded. The dossier inventory omitted section 1, so it is corrected to the five sections of the order. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 and was carried out when the order issued on 1973-01-24. Sections 1 to 4 have no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The held U.S. Code text of 38 U.S.C. 4212 prints Ex. Ord. No. 11701 in its notes, the held eCFR text of 20 CFR 654.8 (amended through 2026-10-30) refers to the mandatory listing program provided by 38 U.S.C. 2012 and Executive Order 11701, the held 48 CFR 22.1300 (through 2026-10-19) lists Executive Order 11701 among the sources of the veterans employment rules, and 31 CFR 202.4 and 203.6 cite it. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and found no amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 11701.
savings_reason: Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 outright with no savings or transitional proviso in the held text, so no residual of EO 11598 is preserved by this order. Sections 1 to 4 have not ended, so no residual from an ended clause exists; the bounded searches found none.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end in sections 1 to 4. A search of the held texts for the number 11701 finds the 1989 OFR codification, current CFR texts and Federal Register rules that cite it; none revokes, supersedes or amends it, and the ofr_catalog search returned no hit. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 on the date the order was issued, 1973-01-24, the order's own date; the end of that clause is from the order's own text and date.
scope_check: The five sections of the order are the corrected inventory (sections 1 to 5); the dossier inventory omitted section 1, so inventory overrides replace the dossier rows with spans cut from the held 38 FR 2675 original.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 to 4 are separate continuing commands (agency job listing rules, statutory delegation, information and reports, procurement rules and cooperation); none has its own date or condition and none was ended by a later instrument found. Section 5 is a one-time supersession of EO 11598 performed on issuance and does not end the other sections.
savings_check: Section 5 contains no savings clause for EO 11598; the other sections are operative so no residual arises from them.

research_rationale: EO 10849 (24 FR 9559, signed 1959-11-27) recites that the Administrator of NASA caused a seal to be made, describes its design, and approves it as the official seal of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation clause. One later instrument acts on it: EO 10942 (signed 1961-05-19; held 26 FR 4419) amends EO 10849 by revising the description of the design of the seal, replacing the description of the shadow cast by the wings as gray-blue with brown; the approval of the seal and its status as the official seal are not changed. The held eCFR text of 14 CFR 1221.102 (amended through 2026-10-15) states that the NASA Seal was established by EO 10849 as amended by EO 10942 (that text gives the amending order's Federal Register cite and date differently from the held Federal Register page, which is 26 FR 4419 for an order signed 1961-05-19), and the held U.S. Code text of 51 U.S.C. 20111 prints the order in its notes. The held texts attributed to EO 10850 and EO 10854 are Federal Register page extracts with no provision affecting EO 10849 (EO 10850's held page begins with EO 10849 itself). the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: No savings clause in the original; the clause has not ended, so no residual exists. The EO 10942 amendment replaced only the design description and left the approval unchanged.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end. EO 10942 amends rather than ends the order (it revises the design description). The held reading of 14 CFR 1221.102 confirms the seal remains established under the order as amended. EO 10850 and EO 10854 held texts contain no change provision for EO 10849.
scope_check: The order is one approval of one seal, treated as a single clause (EO:10849#whole), the whole text of the held Federal Register original.
independent_command_check: There is a single command, the approval of the seal; the design description is part of it and was amended by EO 10942 without ending the approval.
savings_check: No savings clause and no residual from an ended clause.

research_rationale: EO 11141 (29 FR 2477, signed 1964-02-12) declares it the policy of the Executive Branch that contractors and subcontractors on Federal contracts shall not discriminate in employment because of age except on the basis of a bona fide occupational qualification, retirement plan or statutory requirement, and shall not specify a maximum age limit in solicitations or advertisements for employees on Government contracts except on the same basis; it directs the head of each department and agency to take appropriate action to enunciate the policy and directs that the Federal Procurement Regulations and the Armed Services Procurement Regulation be amended to give continuous notice of it. The held Federal Register original has no sunset, condition or revocation clause. The held eCFR text of 48 CFR 22.901 (FAR, amended through 2026-10-19) restates the policy as the Government policy under Executive Order 11141, and the held eCFR texts of 32 CFR 191.1 and 191.5, 18 CFR 1316.6 and 23 CFR 260.115 and the 5 U.S.C. 3301 note (Ex. Ord. No. 11141) cite or print it. the bounded machine searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog were read for coverage and show no amendment, revocation or supersession.
savings_reason: No savings clause in the original and no ended clause. The instruction to amend the FPR and ASPR was carried into the Federal Acquisition Regulation (48 CFR 22.901) rather than ended; no held source dates a performance end, so it is not claimed as terminated.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end. A search of the held texts for the number 11141 finds the 1989 OFR codification, current CFR texts and a Federal Register page; none revokes, supersedes or amends it, and the ofr_catalog search returned no hit.
scope_check: The order is a single paragraph of policy and directions, treated as one clause (EO:11141#whole), the whole order text in the held 29 FR 2477 original.
independent_command_check: The agency enunciation and regulation-amendment directions serve the declared policy; the held 48 CFR 22.901 shows the policy statement continuing in current procurement regulation, and no instrument ends any part.
savings_check: No savings clause and no residual from an ended clause.
